name: Dwarven Digging
summary: At Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof fears the dwarves' digging will anger Mulgore's beasts and scar its sacred earth. He asks young Horde defenders to break the prospectors' picks and halt their work.

sections.title: Trespassers in the Hills
sections.body: Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have marked out a dig site in Mulgore's hills. The Explorer's League searches Kalimdor for titan relics and secrets of the earthen, often without regard for the lands or customs of those who live there. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother, worthy of reverence rather than excavation for stone and metal.

sections.title: Defending the Sacred Earth
sections.body: Baine Bloodhoof sees the dwarves' machines and blasting as a threat to the plains' fragile balance. Their noise agitates the local wildlife and stirs the kodos into frenzy. The tauren mean to smash the prospectors' picks at the forges, sending a blunt warning and stopping the digging before it causes lasting harm.

faq.q: Why are dwarves digging in Mulgore?
faq.answer: Dwarven prospectors search Mulgore for hidden secrets and artifacts beneath the earth. Their mining disregards tauren territory and customs, bringing them into conflict with the tauren.

faq.q: Who gives the quest Dwarven Digging?
faq.answer: Baine Bloodhoof gives the request at Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. He is the young son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof.

faq.q: Why does Baine want their tools smashed instead of just stolen?
faq.answer: Baine wants the picks broken so the excavation stops at once. Destroying them at the forges warns the dwarves that brute force will not win the land's secrets.

faq.q: How does the digging affect the wildlife of Mulgore?
faq.answer: The digging and scars in the earth agitate Mulgore's native creatures, especially the kodos roaming the hills. Peaceful herds grow irritable and aggressive.

faq.q: Where can the picks be smashed?
faq.answer: You can smash the picks at a working forge. The dwarven excavation camp has one, and the blacksmiths in Thunder Bluff have another.

faq.q: Does this quest tie into the larger Explorer's League presence in Kalimdor?
faq.answer: Yes. Dwarven expeditions from Ironforge have outposts across Kalimdor, including Mulgore, the Barrens, and Southern Kalimdor. Their claims to land and sacred ground often bring them into skirmishes with Horde peoples.

angles.text: As a tauren, you know the Earth Mother's body is sacred. Foreigners boring into Mulgore's steppes demand a firm response.
As a member of the Horde, you see Alliance dwarves crossing into Horde lands as a threat to the fragile peace since the Third War and a disregard for tribal borders.
As a shaman, you know careless digging disturbs the bedrock, unsettles the elements, and stirs unrest among the land's spirits and creatures.
As a miner, you may value what lies in stone, but the dwarves' work in Mulgore ignores respect and harmony for reckless destruction.
